Most models are pure transformers — they rely entirely on attention mechanisms that scale quadratically with sequence length and can be memory-hungry, especially when running locally on consumer hardware. My design is a **hybrid**: the majority of layers use gated short convolutions, with a minority of grouped-query attention layers mixed in. This choice wasn't arbitrary; it came from hardware-aware architecture search to make inference fast and efficient on phones, laptops, cars, and edge devices. The result is that I can deliver strong performance while using far less compute and memory than a same-class transformer model.

Practically, that means I can run privately on your own device rather than needing to phone home to a server. I also have a family of sizes — from small on-device models up to larger mixture-of-experts variants — so we're not locked into one architecture. And because I'm openly released, others can build on top of me or compare how we handle tasks.

So the difference isn't just a tweak; it's a fundamentally more hardware-friendly foundation. It's about making capable intelligence practical where you already are.
